title: Lead a team, plan, allocate and assess their work

lessons.title: Planning the team's work
lessons.html:
The team leader's job

A team leader on a farm, whether a foreman in the orchard, a shed supervisor or a livestock team leader, turns the manager's instructions into daily work. You plan the work, give each person a task, check progress and quality, and look after the team's safety and wellbeing.

Start with the objective

Get clear instructions from the manager. A useful objective says what, how much, by when and to what standard. For example: Prune blocks 3 and 4 (1,200 trees) by Friday, removing dead wood and lifting skirts to knee height.

Break the job into tasks

  1. List the tasks: collecting tools, pruning, pulling branches to the row, chipping, checking quality.
  2. Estimate how long each task takes. Use past records: if a worker prunes about 40 trees a day on this kind of block, 1,200 trees need about 30 worker-days.
  3. Work out how many people and how much equipment you need each day.
  4. Check for constraints: weather, other jobs needing the same people or tractor, public holidays, leave.
  5. Put the tasks in order and set daily targets.

Prepare resources

  • Tools sharpened and counted, PPE available, first aid box stocked.
  • Transport arranged to and from the block.
  • Water and toilets available near the work site.
  • Records or tablets ready for recording output.

Identify risks

Before work starts, think about what could go wrong: injuries from saws and ladders, heat stress, bees in the trees, equipment breakdowns. Plan how to prevent them and what to do if they happen. Write a simple plan that you can share with the team and with your manager.

lessons.title: Allocating work and leading the team
lessons.html:
Giving out the work

Allocation means deciding who does what. A good allocation uses people's skills, shares the load fairly and develops people over time.

  • Match tasks to skills and training. Only trained, authorised workers may operate tractors, chippers or sprayers.
  • Pair a new worker with an experienced one.
  • Share hard or unpleasant tasks fairly; rotate them.
  • Consider people's health and any limits they have reported.
  • Give each person or group a clear area and target, such as rows 1 to 10, about 40 trees.

Briefing the team

Hold a short briefing at the start of the day. Explain the objective, the targets, the quality standard and the safety rules. Show what a good result looks like. Ask questions to check understanding, and let people raise concerns.

Leading during the day

  • Be present. Walk the work site regularly.
  • Give praise for good work and correct problems early, calmly and in private.
  • Solve problems quickly: move people if one area finishes early, call for repairs if equipment breaks.
  • Watch for unsafe behaviour and stop it immediately.
  • Treat everyone with respect and apply rules consistently.

Assessing the work

Assessment checks whether the work met the objective.

CheckExample
QuantityTrees pruned per worker and per day vs target
QualitySample 10 trees per row: correct cuts, no stumps, skirts at height
TimeOn schedule for Friday?
SafetyInjuries, near misses, PPE use

Give feedback to individuals and the team. Where work is below standard, find the cause: unclear instruction, lack of skill, poor tools or poor effort. Then act, by retraining, fixing tools or following disciplinary procedure where needed. Report results to your manager, with reasons for any shortfall and suggestions for next time.

Key points

  • Start from a clear objective: what, how much, by when, to what standard.
  • Break work into tasks, estimate time and plan people and equipment.
  • Allocate by skill and fairness; only authorised workers on machinery.
  • Brief the team, stay present and deal with problems early.
  • Assess quantity, quality, time and safety, then give feedback and report.

quiz.question: What does a useful work objective include?

options.text: What, how much, by when and to what standard
Only the name of the block
The names of workers to discipline
The manager's opinion of the team

quiz.question: Work in a block is below standard. What should the leader do first?

options.text: Find the cause, such as unclear instructions, lack of skill or poor tools
Ignore it if the target number was met
Redo it personally without telling anyone
